So I called for a Bosch technician. He came the next day. His response to the wet interior was that dishwashers are meant to wash not dry dishes. Be aware that if you have something delivered or installed by Costco, and it causes $35,000 damage to your home (Disaster Company estimate), they will NOT take responsibility and will defer and deflect. As a 40 year Executive member of Costco, I cannot believe how awful their level of customer relations and service is! A total nightmare that ruined our Christmas and now we are weeks if not MONTHS from getting a functional kitchen, new flooring, and having our lives put back together.

Sentence (English): My previous dishwasher was a 2 year old Whirlpool that came with our new house.
Comments (English): [ Read the HomeConnect privacy policy very carefully ] || ---------------- || My previous dishwasher was a 2 year old Whirlpool that came with our new house. At 50 dBA both my husband and I felt it was way too noisy. It also didn't have a third shelf and was the wrong color. I shopped at the BestBuy Marysville, WA Store with excellent Customer Service. I thought I'd splurge on a new dishwasher made by Bosch. Bosch seems to occupy several top spots in Consumer Reports. I ended up buying this model. **Positives: The white color matches my white kitchen cabinets really well. The door is staying clean, no fingerprints. The third shelf is well designed and much appreciated. * Loading: For the first time in decades I'm stumped. Even after watching the video from the company I'm still having problems loading this thing. It's the most awkward arrangement of tines I've ever come across. I have to load and reload…. and load and reload! Who ever came up with this array needs lessons in practicality. * Cleaning: dishes come out very clean, but not as clean as Bosch would like you to believe. Occasionally there's a bit stuck to my cereal bowl and also a bit of egg yolk on the plate. That's not a big deal and easy enough to fix. I continue to pre-rinse. Amazingly enough I find the short 60 min cycle to be as efficient as the much longer cycles. No need to overdo it! * Noise: Previous reviewers mentioned how quiet this dishwasher is at 42 dBA. I however, can hear this dishwasher across the room. It's quieter than the Whirlpool I owned before, but not by much. I've owned other brands in the past that were quieter than this Bosch. Big disappointment! * Drying: When the cycle is done (any cycle) the dishes are not dry, and the inside of the door is still sopping wet. I then open up the dishwasher, shake all the water off the plastics, wipe down the edges of the rails, wipe down the door, and then prop the door open with a long rubber spoon. The reason I have to prop the door open to let steam escape is because the door stays in 2 positions only: wide open, or shut. If you try to stop anywhere in between, the door will snap shut. Generally the dishes are pretty dry 30 minutes after I prop the door open. * Wi-Fi: if you want to connect to Wifi you need to first download the HomeConnect app. If you plan on doing that, please read the . “Data protection and privacy Information“ chapter very very carefully. You have to “volunteer” an awful lot of your private info in order to run this app. It definitely isn't worth the convenience you get by using wifi. This isn't just disappointing, it's appalling. I deleted the app, I never connected it. I feel so ripped off! I feel a customer should be able to run an app without info being collected about how you use the dishwasher, how hard your water is, how often you use the cycles, etc etc. Providing all that info should be optional, not mandatory! **Final words: The rating I am giving this is 2.5. All in all I consider this dishwasher to be an engineering design failure. It takes much more time to load than any other dishwasher I've owned. Drying is so mediocre that it takes a medium size dish drying cloth to sop up the leftover water. Since I value my privacy I can't run the WiFi option. The negatives outweigh the positives, and therefore I can't recommend this dishwasher.

Comments (English): [ Long Installation Time, Ended Up Faulty. ] || ---------------- || Purchased from Lowe's just before Thanksgiving, was delivered on Nov. 27th. Called the installer the next day to come check it out to make sure the leak wasn't due to installation, which he graciously checked, and we found the seal issue. Called Lowe's support for Whirlpool and which point (Dec. 15th) I was told I couldn't get a service technician until Dec. 28th. I shouldn't be shuffled into an installation schedule, faulty equipment should get quick and immediate attention. Not a great first Whirlpool experience. Hopefully the replacement works better.

Sentence (English): Look, the concept of a portable dishwasher is already kind of raggedy.
Comments (English): [ Better than no dishwasher, yet a chore to use ] || ---------------- || Look, the concept of a portable dishwasher is already kind of raggedy. It's a big rolling appliance that requires a bunch of steps and prerequisites—as many as a built-in, just a little less invasive cabinetry-wise. If you're using one, you're probably in an older house. Are you really going to install its own dedicated outlet within reach of the short cord? No, you'll have to use the shortest 14/3 extension cord you can get away with. You're also not supposed to use these things with a side sprayer or pull down faucet—people do anyway but I don't want a hose rupture so I installed a different faucet. Ok fine. But then the adapter that GE provides to connect the Unicouple doesn't aerate. It makes your kitchen faucet violent and messy like a garden hose. Should be fun when I am doing anything at my kitchen sink but using the dishwasher! Speaking of which, the Unicouple leaks. This I do not understand. Two OEM parts—Unicouple and adapter—and it LEAKS. A $600 appliance. None of the solutions in the manual helped.Even the $80 handheld bidet attached to my bathroom sink faucet aerates the water when it's not diverted, and doesn't leak at the connection when it is diverted. So why can't GE make their OEM parts not leak when used as intended? I just feel like this is job #1 for plumbing-related appliances: don't leak.I know it sounds like I only have complaints…not so. My dishes were perfectly clean and fairly dry, except where water pooled —normal. You should use rinse aid for dry dishes. A cycle took about 2 hours.If you are pre-rinsing and not getting clean dishes, that's user error and a waste of water. Scrape your plate and do NOT pre-rinse—you're playing life on hard mode. The sensor needs to see soil to do its work.

Sentence (English): We renovated our house and our designer suggested this model dishwasher and matching refrigerator to make our stove the centerpiece of the room.
Comments (English): [ It gets the job done but misses the mark ] || ---------------- || We renovated our house and our designer suggested this model dishwasher and matching refrigerator to make our stove the centerpiece of the room. The black stainless helps it to blend with our dark cabinets. This unit is pretty quiet but the annoying thing is how hard it is to fit in wine glasses and sheet pans or cookware at the same time. You can lower the rack but then you can't fit in sheet pans. You can raise the rack but you can't fit in wine glasses. The annoying workaround is to remove the upper cutlery shelf so you can then do both but they should have made the rack differently for the stemware. We have had it for a few months and now it makes an annoying groaning noise when you close the door. Looking online, this seems to be a spring issue and we are about to call out service to get it repaired. We miss our Bosch as it cleaned really well and was easier to work with but they don't come in black stainless.

Sentence (English): I replaced my 15 yo Bosch d/w with this new one as it had a few nice features, i.e. interior light (yay), WiFi and water softener dispenser (salt) and time remaining displays on the floor.
Comments (English): [ Bosch Benchmark DW shx9pcm5n ] || ---------------- || I replaced my 15 yo Bosch d/w with this new one as it had a few nice features, i.e. interior light (yay), WiFi and water softener dispenser (salt) and time remaining displays on the floor.So far the cleaning has been fabulous! Spotless! It sort of freaks me out that the cycles are soooo long. Auto with drying is over 3 hours! It is dead quiet though :)- the light on the floor with remaining time is important and a big improvement over just the red light on the floor. It is nice to get a text that the cycle is done.However I hesitate to give it 5 stars for several reasons:- the light on the floor and on the interior display does not say 'finished/clean/sanitized'. This is super frustrating.I would like the light on the floor to say 'clean' when done and stay on until the door is opened. Hoping since it is connected to WiFi that a simple software update could me made? Also, the new third rack for small items/utensils is nice, however the regular silverware basket has been downsized and it is too small. I like pulling the silverware basket out onto the counter to put away silverware. I do wish they added a large liquid soap dispenser so you didn't have to add soap every time.The WiFi feature is frankly useless unless there are software updates. I don't think I need to remotely start a dishwasher .I love the cleaning power which is the entire purpose of a D/W i just wish some of the improved features were a bit more advanced.The handles match my Bosch fridge, over and micro (old DW did not). Nice.

Sentence (English): I love my new Bosch dishwasher!
Comments (English): [ Great performance, great deal! ] || ---------------- || I love my new Bosch dishwasher! I put up with a malfunctioning dishwasher that left crusty residue on glasses and ceramic bowls for over two years. I rearranged my loading, took the obnoxiously designed thing apart several times to clean the "filter", and enlisted a certified dishwasher repairman who told me to use a certain type of dishwasher pod (I did). Nothing helped. When Costco offered a Bosch with a $300 discount we went for it! We did our research and were confident a Bosch was our best bet. We have not been disappointed. The thing is crazy quiet and the old dishes and glassware sparkle and look almost new again. We've put gross baked on sauce and cheese encrusting casserole pans in to test our Bosch's real efficiency. They always come out clean. The filter is super easy to reach and rinse and really hasn't had anything in it so far. The plastic is frequently dry, but not always. I'm fine with it though as paying a $1000 more not to dry a container or two isn't worth it to me! For the money, reliability rating and performance, I'd say Bosch is the best!

Sentence (English): My previous dishwasher was a 2 year old Whirlpool that came with our new house.
Comments (English): [ Read the HomeConnect privacy policy very carefully ] || ---------------- || My previous dishwasher was a 2 year old Whirlpool that came with our new house. At 50 dBA both my husband and I felt it was way too noisy. It also didn't have a third shelf and was the wrong color.I shopped at the BestBuy Marysville, WA Store with excellent Customer Service. I thought I'd splurge on a new dishwasher made by Bosch. Bosch seems to occupy several top spots in Consumer Reports. I ended up buying this model. **Positives: The white color matches my white kitchen cabinets really well. The door is staying clean, no fingerprints. The third shelf is well designed and much appreciated. * Loading: For the first time in decades I'm stumped. Even after watching the video from the company I'm still having problems loading this thing. It's the most awkward arrangement of tines I've ever come across. I have to load and reload…. and load and reload! Who ever came up with this array needs lessons in practicality. * Cleaning: dishes come out very clean, but not as clean as Bosch would like you to believe. Occasionally there's a bit stuck to my cereal bowl and also a bit of egg yolk on the plate. That's not a big deal and easy enough to fix. I continue to pre-rinse. Amazingly enough I find the short 60 min cycle to be as efficient as the much longer cycles. No need to overdo it! * Noise: Previous reviewers mentioned how quiet this dishwasher is at 42 dBA. I however, can hear this dishwasher across the room. It's quieter than the Whirlpool I owned before, but not by much. I've owned other brands in the past that were quieter than this Bosch. Big disappointment! * Drying: When the cycle is done (any cycle) the dishes are not dry, and the inside of the door is still sopping wet. I then open up the dishwasher, shake all the water off the plastics, wipe down the edges of the rails, wipe down the door, and then prop the door open with a long rubber spoon. The reason I have to prop the door open to let steam escape is because the door stays in 2 positions only: wide open, or shut. If you try to stop anywhere in between, the door will snap shut. Generally the dishes are pretty dry 30 minutes after I prop the door open.* Wi-Fi: if you want to connect to Wifi you need to first download the HomeConnect app. If you plan on doing that, please read the “Data protection and privacy Information“ chapter very very carefully. You have to “volunteer” an awful lot of your private info in order to run this app. It definitely isn't worth the convenience you get by using wifi. This isn't just disappointing, it's appalling. I deleted the app, I never connected it. I feel so ripped off! I feel a customer should be able to run an app without info being collected about how you use the dishwasher, how hard your water is, how often you use the cycles, etc etc. Providing all that info should be optional, not mandatory! **Final words: The rating I am giving this is 2.5. All in all I consider this dishwasher to be an engineering design failure. It takes much more time to load than any other dishwasher I've owned. Drying is so mediocre that it takes a medium size dish drying cloth to sop up the leftover water. Since I value my privacy I can't run the WiFi option. The negatives outweigh the positives, and therefore I can't recommend this dishwasher.

Sentence (English): This is my second Bosch dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Super quiet! ] || ---------------- || This is my second Bosch dishwasher. After moving and having to leave my first behind, we chose Bosch when we had to replace our existing dishwasher. I went with the top model featuring the CrystalDry Technology. Not having to deal with wet spots when emptying it sounded nice. The unit cleans beautifully. After using now for a couple of months, I have not had any dish not come out completely clean. The CrystalDry feature, though, is not performing as it claims. I do have dishes that come out with some standing water. It is better than the average dishwasher as far as completely drying things, but not enough that had I known, I would have paid extra for. The reviews I read stated it worked perfectly which is why I went with the more expensive model. But reality is I still have some standing water after running a cycle. I do use rinse aid as instructed. But overall, I am very happy with this Bosch dishwasher. Cleans great and super, super quiet.

Sentence (English): This was a replacement for a Bosch dishwasher that was great.
Comments (English): This was a replacement for a Bosch dishwasher that was great. The old one developed an error code (E15) after 8 years of use. I really liked how quiet it was and it did a great job cleaning the dishes. When I needed to replace it, I didn't hesitate to get another Bosch. Unfortunately, the new one isn't as good. It is still very quiet, but it doesn't display the amount of time remaining in the cycle. The only way to know the time remaining is to install the app. And then, when the cycle is complete, the “clean” light comes on, but only for a few minutes. Then the display is completely blank. So, several times already in just two months, someone in the household has loaded dirty dishes in a load of clean dishes, not knowing that it needed to be emptied of the clean dishes. I can't find a way in the app to keep the “clean” light on after the cycle. I specifically bought the model with the front display to show the cycle time and when the cycle was complete. It seems like a step backwards for Bosch on the dishwasher.

Sentence (English): I replaced my 15 yo Bosch d/w with this new one as it had a few nice features, i.e. interior light (yay), WiFi and water softener dispenser (salt) and time remaining displays on the floor.
Comments (English): [ Bosch Benchmark DW shx9pcm5n ] || ---------------- || I replaced my 15 yo Bosch d/w with this new one as it had a few nice features, i.e. interior light (yay), WiFi and water softener dispenser (salt) and time remaining displays on the floor. So far the cleaning has been fabulous! Spotless! It sort of freaks me out that the cycles are soooo long. Auto with drying is over 3 hours! It is dead quiet though :)- the light on the floor with remaining time is important and a big improvement over just the red light on the floor. It is nice to get a text that the cycle is done. However I hesitate to give it 5 stars for several reasons: - the light on the floor and on the interior display does not say 'finished/clean/sanitized'. This is super frustrating.I would like the light on the floor to say 'clean' when done and stay on until the door is opened. Hoping since it is connected to WiFi that a simple software update could me made? Also, the new third rack for small items/utensils is nice, however the regular silverware basket has been downsized and it is too small. I like pulling the silverware basket out onto the counter to put away silverware. I do wish they added a large liquid soap dispenser so you didn't have to add soap every time. The WiFi feature is frankly useless unless there are software updates. I don't think I need to remotely start a dishwasher . I love the cleaning power which is the entire purpose of a D/W i just wish some of the improved features were a bit more advanced. The handles match my Bosch fridge, over and micro (old DW did not). Nice.

I didn't want to take a chance and order another one so I opted to call technical services and they sent a repair company out to the house, about 2 weeks later. They are third party contractors who won't answer calls and Lowe's customer service is terrible beyond reckoning. The experience was so frustrating and rude that we're getting the rest of our appliances elsewhere. The dishwasher is fine enough and Lowe's is terrible.

Comments (English): [ Almost Perfect ] || ---------------- || The big thing is: it's quiet and cleans really well. The auto-air ensures that washed articles are dried effectively. I'm very satisfied.The niggles were annoying, but minor: • The front feet were difficult to adjust. Your competitors do a much better job with this. • The 500-series top controls eliminated the "time remaining" LED window that appears on my friend's 300-series model. While this may be an improvement for repair issues, it's not as user-friendly as we like being able to see the time remaining. • The description of this unit says it can run a "Machine Clean" cycle for (occasional) deep cleaning. The main user manual mentions this as well, as does the 500-series supplemental owner's manual. This cycle is apparently accessed through the Home Connect app. The problems are a) I cannot find how to access it in Home Connect, and b) I emailed you for assistance, and received a prompt and polite reply, which told me that this feature was accessed through Home Connect. but was *not* included in the 500 model. This isn't a deal-killer, but it's annoying to be misled by Bosche's own written materials. • The included cutlery basket was annoyingly small, far far smaller than the larger basket in my friend's Bosch dishwasher. Like the omission of the "time remaining" LEDs, I found this an unwanted cheapening. I remedied the too-small basket by buying a bigger Bosch cutlery basket. which I had to find in the aftermarket because the bigger basket in the Bosch on-line listing was "out of stock" and "unavailable."

Sentence (English): We bought our quadwash dishwasher in early 2020 off the internet and were blown away with its features compared to other popular euro brands.
Comments (English): [ Brilliant spec on paper and when working but.  ] || ---------------- || We bought our quadwash dishwasher in early 2020 off the internet and were blown away with its features compared to other popular euro brands. It's quiet, easy to clean, has highly configurable baskets and the steam clean function really works well when it's needed. Bought off the interned and not seen in the showroom, once we started using it we quickly noticed that the display and buttons are hidden from view when the door was closed and so we removed the lid to see key info like the cycle time remaining when running. No biggie but a silly move by the designer to prioritise form over function. After 11 months of daily use the machine had a fatal error and it wouldn't drain 'OE' error on the display. The repair done under warranty was to replace the heater and pump module which required an hour of dismantling and reassembly. The repairman told me that the new part was over 300 dollars and close inspection showed a burned out bimetallic switch on a heater element. After the repair it was working as it should. After 28 months of use we noticed the plastic elements of the baskets and top tray cracking or breaking off altogether. All this ocurred over about three months and we never changed from our regular Woolworths Shine powder. The loss of the plastic brackets caused the racks to collapse and eventually dislodge, causing the plates to collapse when loaded. The top tray tines that hold the forks also started breaking easily, so it became a pain to use. I tried to buy replacement baskets at 100-200 dollars each from LG parts resellers THREE TIMES and each time my order was cancelled and refunded. The final time the reseller told me that LG were out of stock with a four month ETA. Big fail for a dishwasher of this calibre. Then in the last week, after nearly four years of twice-daily use the machine has started throwing an water inlet error 'IE' and the cycle stops before the final rinse. TBF I'm done with this unit and looking back over the last twelve years we've used Miele, Bosch and Neff dishwashers in our previous houses that were of a lower spec but after several years of hard use had never showed any signs of failure or wear like this LG dishwasher has. In short I would have expected this top of the range dishwasher to have stood the test of time but alas I fear that a repair and basket refresh will cost over a thousand dollars and that would otherwise practically get me a new dishwasher that will give more than four years of use if I'm lucky. It's going to hurt me to do this as it's not a sustainable approach but we need a working dishwasher 24h/day (not four months ETA! ) and so it is what it is. At least if I buy one of the other euro brands of dishwasher I'll be able to get replacement parts for it!

Sentence (English): My biggest complaint was the ridiculous design of the fill container on the left side of DW.
Comments (English): [ Possibility to flood outside unit ] || ---------------- || My biggest complaint was the ridiculous design of the fill container on the left side of DW. The rubber hose comes out of the electronically controlled fill valve and basically just gravity feeds into the unit from the side. This port isn't sealed on the top so steam comes out as the unit fills and goes under the cabinets. Also, during installation this fill port container has the ability to rotate to any position. If it is not at the twelve o'clock position the water will go right out the top of the container and onto your floor. Very very poor design. Ask me how I know? Yup, flooded under the unit and onto my wood floors during first cycle. Pulled unit back out and discovered this design flaw. Ended up securing this gravity feed fill container with speed tape in the upright position. Also secured the rubber hose to the side of the unit. Worked great after this engineering tweak.

I can run this thing and you can't even hear it running. The one I had before sounded like a jet airplane taking off. On the downside is the price, for $1,400 gets you ultra quiet dishwashers like this, but for the $600 price range you can still get a really nice dishwasher that is quite. On the other hand I bought this dishwasher specifically for the Crystal Dry feature, which is really cool technology and really does dry the dishes really well, so I can't complain about that. The other selling point for me was how the dishwasher has a tub underneath in case of any leaks, so that is a great benefit and what really sold me on this dishwasher since I know it won't cause water damage in my kitchen. I am work in I.T. as a cyber security engineer and I couldn't get the dishwasher added to the phone. For $1,400 I would expect a better working app, especially since some of the controls can ONLY be done through the app. However, I expect this to improve over time as the software engineering team at Bosch gets a User Story created to work out the bugs. Overall great dishwasher and gets a 5 star in my book.

Sentence (English): The big thing is: it's quiet and cleans really well.
Comments (English): [ Almost Perfect ] || ---------------- || The big thing is: it's quiet and cleans really well. The auto-air ensures that washed articles are dried effectively. I'm very satisfied. The niggles were annoying, but minor: • The front feet were difficult to adjust. Your competitors do a much better job with this. • The 500-series top controls eliminated the "time remaining" LED window that appears on my friend's 300-series model. While this may be an improvement for repair issues, it's not as user-friendly as we like being able to see the time remaining. • The description of this unit says it can run a "Machine Clean" cycle for (occasional) deep cleaning. The main user manual mentions this as well, as does the 500-series supplemental owner's manual. This cycle is apparently accessed through the Home Connect app. The problems are a) I cannot find how to access it in Home Connect, and b) I emailed you for assistance, and received a prompt and polite reply, which told me that this feature was accessed through Home Connect. but was *not* included in the 500 model. This isn't a deal-killer, but it's annoying to be misled by Bosche's own written materials. • The included cutlery basket was annoyingly small, far far smaller than the larger basket in my friend's Bosch dishwasher. Like the omission of the "time remaining" LEDs, I found this an unwanted cheapening. I remedied the too-small basket by buying a bigger Bosch cutlery basket. which I had to find in the aftermarket because the bigger basket in the Bosch on-line listing was "out of stock" and "unavailable."

Sentence (English): So far, dishwasher works well: washes, dries (reasonably) and is very quiet; the rack organization is reasonable.
Comments (English): So far, dishwasher works well: washes, dries (reasonably) and is very quiet; the rack organization is reasonable. However, there are a few significant problematic points: First, setting up Home Connect was quite painful – the process of using Bluetooth to connect the device, wifi and my phone was excruciating. The basic instructions are extremely primitive. Only after endless hours of troubleshooting and research, I discovered that a. my phone needed to be on wifi only – i.e., the wireless phone carrier signal needed to be turned off, and b. my extender needed to be turned off (or renamed). Who naturally has their phone on wifi only? And many people use extenders that don't have a separate name from their router. And while this was not my issue, the DW will only work on 2.4GHz, not 5 GHz. And when you finally can detect the router, the setup shows only the router with the best connection (if you live in an apartment building, there can be a dozen other routers with stronger signals than yours) – to see the other ones, you have to click on that router; this also is not obvious at all. These are such common traps that they should be presented upfront and obviously, and should not simply buried in FAQ. Better yet fix the set-up so that these aren't issues. Many might be just as happy to not use Home Connect, but the extra featured cycles (that you pay for if you have a 300, 500, 800+) are available only thru the app – extremely annoying.Next, and probably the bigger issue, since the former was solvable, when the dishwasher runs it emits a harsh chemical odor, which after some online research, is best identified as a tar smell. At first I thought burning rubber, and got very concerned, but there was no smoking or visible haze. It seems numerous users have encountered a similar smell over the years and they identify it as the result of bitumen (an asphalt related substance) in the insulation heating up during use. (Sadly, I hope this is the issue and not something even worse. It definitely is not because of food build-up or such – the smell was noticed around the third use and no food scraps go into the DW.) I hadn't noticed this the first few washes, because I set the DW and then left the kitchen. In my case, the smell dissipates relatively quickly, but it is clearly noticeable within a 3-5 feet radius – the smell comes from between the door / control panel top edge and the countertop. It seems for other users the smell can be overpowering. To try to minimize this, we typically run the DW at delicate (lower temps), eco and half-load, to reduce heat and running time. This is not a trivial issue, and seems very common. We don't need toxic chemicals in the house. It's been over 2 months, and the smell hasn't disappeared as a “new appliance” smell. I don't understand why Bosch won't correct it.Also, installation-wise there's got to be a better mounting system. The pieces included don't work for top mounting with stone / marble counters, unless you want to drill in (bad idea). The side mount doesn't work well and is very fiddly. And based on the weight distribution and the requirement of gap space, unless the DW is secured firmly, the whole appliance will tilt if you try to open the door. This is another design flaw that should be fixed.Other issues: The bottom surface of the tub has a few areas that are depressed and will collect water that sits even when the cycle is over. Given the importance of keeping the interior of tub as dry as possible to prevent mold etc., it's not clear why these areas are necessary and the design can't be adjusted. The user manual tells you that the drain hose must at some point be at least 33 inches high. But that's the dishwasher height. Most countertops will be at 34 inches. Who has the adjacent space higher than that? And most people will have the drain hose reside under the sink, where there is a sink basin. We manage to have it at about 32, but that was hard to accomplish. Bosch (or the Home Depot) should also make very clear in product presentation materials that the three prong connector is included but a separate connector must be purchased for hardwiring – it takes too much research to find this out before purchase (and it's clear others have missed it until the installers arrive).While in some respects the DW seems very good, these other issues are substantial and known (or knowable) and seem eminently correctable.

It seems numerous users have encountered a similar smell over the years and they identify it as the result of bitumen (an asphalt related substance) in the insulation heating up during use. The pieces included don't work for top mounting with stone / marble counters, unless you want to drill in (bad idea). The side mount doesn't work well and is very fiddly. However, there are a few significant problematic points: First, setting up Home Connect was quite painful – the process of using Bluetooth to connect the device, wifi and my phone was excruciating. The basic instructions are extremely primitive. Only after endless hours of troubleshooting and research, I discovered that a. my phone needed to be on wifi only – i.e., the wireless phone carrier signal needed to be turned off, and b. my extender needed to be turned off (or renamed). Who naturally has their phone on wifi only? And many people use extenders that don't have a separate name from their router. And while this was not my issue, the DW will only work on 2.4GHz, not 5 GHz. And when you finally can detect the router, the setup shows only the router with the best connection (if you live in an apartment building, there can be a dozen other routers with stronger signals than yours) – to see the other ones, you have to click on that router; this also is not obvious at all. These are such common traps that they should be presented upfront and obviously, and should not simply buried in FAQ. Better yet fix the set-up so that these aren't issues. Many might be just as happy to not use Home Connect, but the extra featured cycles (that you pay for if you have a 300, 500, 800+) are available only thru the app – extremely annoying.Next, and probably the bigger issue, since the former was solvable, when the dishwasher runs it emits a harsh chemical odor, which after some online research, is best identified as a tar smell. At first I thought burning rubber, and got very concerned, but there was no smoking or visible haze. It seems numerous users have encountered a similar smell over the years and they identify it as the result of bitumen (an asphalt related substance) in the insulation heating up during use. (Sadly, I hope this is the issue and not something even worse. It definitely is not because of food build-up or such – the smell was noticed around the third use and no food scraps go into the DW.) I hadn't noticed this the first few washes, because I set the DW and then left the kitchen. In my case, the smell dissipates relatively quickly, but it is clearly noticeable within a 3-5 feet radius – the smell comes from between the door / control panel top edge and the countertop. It seems for other users the smell can be overpowering. To try to minimize this, we typically run the DW at delicate (lower temps), eco and half-load, to reduce heat and running time. This is not a trivial issue, and seems very common. We don't need toxic chemicals in the house. It's been over 2 months, and the smell hasn't disappeared as a “new appliance” smell. I don't understand why Bosch won't correct it.Also, installation-wise there's got to be a better mounting system. The pieces included don't work for top mounting with stone / marble counters, unless you want to drill in (bad idea). The side mount doesn't work well and is very fiddly. And based on the weight distribution and the requirement of gap space, unless the DW is secured firmly, the whole appliance will tilt if you try to open the door. This is another design flaw that should be fixed.Other issues: The bottom surface of the tub has a few areas that are depressed and will collect water that sits even when the cycle is over. Given the importance of keeping the interior of tub as dry as possible to prevent mold etc., it's not clear why these areas are necessary and the design can't be adjusted. The user manual tells you that the drain hose must at some point be at least 33 inches high. But that's the dishwasher height. Most countertops will be at 34 inches. Who has the adjacent space higher than that? And most people will have the drain hose reside under the sink, where there is a sink basin. We manage to have it at about 32, but that was hard to accomplish. Bosch (or the Home Depot) should also make very clear in product presentation materials that the three prong connector is included but a separate connector must be purchased for hardwiring – it takes too much research to find this out before purchase (and it's clear others have missed it until the installers arrive).While in some respects the DW seems very good, these other issues are substantial and known (or knowable) and seem eminently correctable.

(Sadly, I hope this is the issue and not something even worse. It definitely is not because of food build-up or such – the smell was noticed around the third use and no food scraps go into the DW.) I hadn’t noticed this the first few washes, because I set the DW and then left the kitchen. In my case, the smell dissipates relatively quickly, but it is clearly noticeable within a 3-5 feet radius – the smell comes from between the door / control panel top edge and the countertop. It seems for other users the smell can be overpowering. To try to minimize this, we typically run the DW at delicate (lower temps), eco and half-load, to reduce heat and running time. This is not a trivial issue, and seems very common. We don’t need toxic chemicals in the house. It’s been over 2 months, and the smell hasn’t disappeared as a “new appliance” smell. I don’t understand why Bosch won’t correct it.Also, installation-wise there’s got to be a better mounting system. The pieces included don’t work for top mounting with stone / marble counters, unless you want to drill in (bad idea). The side mount doesn’t work well and is very fiddly. And based on the weight distribution and the requirement of gap space, unless the DW is secured firmly, the whole appliance will tilt if you try to open the door. This is another design flaw that should be fixed.Other issues: The bottom surface of the tub has a few areas that are depressed and will collect water that sits even when the cycle is over. Given the importance of keeping the interior of tub as dry as possible to prevent mold etc., it’s not clear why these areas are necessary and the design can’t be adjusted. The user manual tells you that the drain hose must at some point be at least 33 inches high. But that’s the dishwasher height. Most countertops will be at 34 inches. Who has the adjacent space higher than that? And most people will have the drain hose reside under the sink, where there is a sink basin. We manage to have it at about 32, but that was hard to accomplish. And while this was not my issue, the DW will only work on 2.4GHz, not 5 GHz. And when you finally can detect the router, the setup shows only the router with the best connection (if you live in an apartment building, there can be a dozen other routers with stronger signals than yours) – to see the other ones, you have to click on that router; this also is not obvious at all. It seems for other users the smell can be overpowering. To try to minimize this, we typically run the DW at delicate (lower temps), eco and half-load, to reduce heat and running time. This is not a trivial issue, and seems very common. We don’t need toxic chemicals in the house. It’s been over 2 months, and the smell hasn’t disappeared as a “new appliance” smell. The pieces included don’t work for top mounting with stone / marble counters, unless you want to drill in (bad idea). The side mount doesn’t work well and is very fiddly. And based on the weight distribution and the requirement of gap space, unless the DW is secured firmly, the whole appliance will tilt if you try to open the door. Given the importance of keeping the interior of tub as dry as possible to prevent mold etc., it’s not clear why these areas are necessary and the design can’t be adjusted. Who naturally has their phone on wifi only? And many people use extenders that don't have a separate name from their router. And while this was not my issue, the DW will only work on 2.4GHz, not 5 GHz. And when you finally can detect the router, the setup shows only the router with the best connection (if you live in an apartment building, there can be a dozen other routers with stronger signals than yours) – to see the other ones, you have to click on that router; this also is not obvious at all. These are such common traps that they should be presented upfront and obviously, and should not simply buried in FAQ. Better yet fix the set-up so that these aren't issues. Many might be just as happy to not use Home Connect, but the extra featured cycles (that you pay for if you have a 300, 500, 800+) are available only thru the app – extremely annoying.Next, and probably the bigger issue, since the former was solvable, when the dishwasher runs it emits a harsh chemical odor, which after some online research, is best identified as a tar smell. At first I thought burning rubber, and got very concerned, but there was no smoking or visible haze. It seems numerous users have encountered a similar smell over the years and they identify it as the result of bitumen (an asphalt related substance) in the insulation heating up during use. (Sadly, I hope this is the issue and not something even worse. It definitely is not because of food build-up or such – the smell was noticed around the third use and no food scraps go into the DW.) I hadn't noticed this the first few washes, because I set the DW and then left the kitchen. In my case, the smell dissipates relatively quickly, but it is clearly noticeable within a 3-5 feet radius – the smell comes from between the door / control panel top edge and the countertop. It seems for other users the smell can be overpowering. To try to minimize this, we typically run the DW at delicate (lower temps), eco and half-load, to reduce heat and running time. This is not a trivial issue, and seems very common. We don't need toxic chemicals in the house. It's been over 2 months, and the smell hasn't disappeared as a “new appliance” smell. I don't understand why Bosch won't correct it.Also, installation-wise there's got to be a better mounting system. The pieces included don't work for top mounting with stone / marble counters, unless you want to drill in (bad idea). The side mount doesn't work well and is very fiddly. And based on the weight distribution and the requirement of gap space, unless the DW is secured firmly, the whole appliance will tilt if you try to open the door. This is another design flaw that should be fixed.Other issues: The bottom surface of the tub has a few areas that are depressed and will collect water that sits even when the cycle is over. Given the importance of keeping the interior of tub as dry as possible to prevent mold etc., it's not clear why these areas are necessary and the design can't be adjusted. The user manual tells you that the drain hose must at some point be at least 33 inches high. But that's the dishwasher height. Most countertops will be at 34 inches. Who has the adjacent space higher than that? And most people will have the drain hose reside under the sink, where there is a sink basin. We manage to have it at about 32, but that was hard to accomplish. Bosch (or the Home Depot) should also make very clear in product presentation materials that the three prong connector is included but a separate connector must be purchased for hardwiring – it takes too much research to find this out before purchase (and it's clear others have missed it until the installers arrive).While in some respects the DW seems very good, these other issues are substantial and known (or knowable) and seem eminently correctable.

The user manual tells you that the drain hose must at some point be at least 33 inches high. But that’s the dishwasher height. Most countertops will be at 34 inches. Who has the adjacent space higher than that? And most people will have the drain hose reside under the sink, where there is a sink basin. We manage to have it at about 32, but that was hard to accomplish. Bosch (or the Home Depot) should also make very clear in product presentation materials that the three prong connector is included but a separate connector must be purchased for hardwiring – it takes too much research to find this out before purchase (and it’s clear others have missed it until the installers arrive).While in some respects the DW seems very good, these other issues are substantial and known (or knowable) and seem eminently correctable.

Sentence (English): So far, dishwasher works well: washes, dries (reasonably) and is very quiet; the rack organization is reasonable.
Comments (English): [ Good washer but tar smell & difficult app setup ] || ---------------- || So far, dishwasher works well: washes, dries (reasonably) and is very quiet; the rack organization is reasonable. However, there are a few significant problematic points: First, setting up Home Connect was quite painful – the process of using Bluetooth to connect the device, wifi and my phone was excruciating. The basic instructions are extremely primitive. Only after endless hours of troubleshooting and research, I discovered that a. my phone needed to be on wifi only – i.e., the wireless phone carrier signal needed to be turned off, and b. my extender needed to be turned off (or renamed). Who naturally has their phone on wifi only? And many people use extenders that don't have a separate name from their router. And while this was not my issue, the DW will only work on 2.4GHz, not 5 GHz. And when you finally can detect the router, the setup shows only the router with the best connection (if you live in an apartment building, there can be a dozen other routers with stronger signals than yours) – to see the other ones, you have to click on that router; this also is not obvious at all. These are such common traps that they should be presented upfront and obviously, and should not simply buried in FAQ. Better yet fix the set-up so that these aren't issues. Many might be just as happy to not use Home Connect, but the extra featured cycles (that you pay for if you have a 300, 500, 800+) are available only thru the app – extremely annoying. Next, and probably the bigger issue, since the former was solvable, when the dishwasher runs it emits a harsh chemical odor, which after some online research, is best identified as a tar smell. At first I thought burning rubber, and got very concerned, but there was no smoking or visible haze. It seems numerous users have encountered a similar smell over the years and they identify it as the result of bitumen (an asphalt related substance) in the insulation heating up during use. (Sadly, I hope this is the issue and not something even worse. It definitely is not because of food build-up or such – the smell was noticed around the third use and no food scraps go into the DW.) I hadn't noticed this the first few washes, because I set the DW and then left the kitchen. In my case, the smell dissipates relatively quickly, but it is clearly noticeable within a 3-5 feet radius – the smell comes from between the door / control panel top edge and the countertop. It seems for other users the smell can be overpowering. To try to minimize this, we typically run the DW at delicate (lower temps), eco and half-load, to reduce heat and running time. This is not a trivial issue, and seems very common. We don't need toxic chemicals in the air in the house. It's been about 2 months, and the smell hasn't disappeared as a “new appliance” smell. I don't understand why Bosch won't correct it. Also, installation-wise there's got to be a better mounting system. The pieces included don't work for top mounting with stone / marble counters, unless you want to drill in (bad idea). The side mount doesn't work well and is very fiddly. And based on the weight distribution and the requirement of gap space, unless the DW is secured firmly, the whole appliance will tilt if you try to open the door. This is another design flaw that should be fixed. Other issues: The bottom surface of the tub has a few areas that are depressed and will collect water that sits even when the cycle is over. Given the importance of keeping the interior of tub as dry as possible to prevent mold etc., it's not clear why these areas are necessary and the design can't be adjusted. The user manual tells you that the drain hose must at some point be at least 33 inches high. But that's the dishwasher height. Most countertops will be at 34 inches. Who has the adjacent space higher than that? And most people will have the drain hose reside under the sink, where there is a sink basin. Bosch (or the Home Depot) should also make very clear in product presentation materials that the three prong connector is included but a separate connector must be purchased for hardwiring – it takes too much research to find this out before purchase (and it's clear others have missed it until the installers arrive). The responsiveness of the control panel buttons can be improved. I usually have to touch the buttons 2 or 3 times before it registers. While in some respects the DW seems very good, these other issues are substantial and known (or knowable) and seem eminently correctable.

Comments (English): [ Buyer Beware - Part Two ] || ---------------- || Bosch did send a representative to check my dishwasher. I thought it was rust that appeared on the boarder of the dishwashing opening. It turned out that Bosch can not clean using Cascade dishwashing pods. The gentleman said I needed to use 1/2 tsp. The Bosch repairman was very courteous but there is no way I would have purchased this dishwasher needed such excessive care. I have to add, after cutting open my Cascade pod and collecting the dish powder and using only a 1/2 teaspoon - the dishes were clean without water spots. Had I known all this along with my original Buyer Beware - no way I would have purchased this dishwasher. Amen.

Sentence (English): I'm worried about my electricity bill because I use a lot of various products, so I check the power usage on the LG ThinQ app.
Comments (English): [Blog] The advantage of the LG DIOS dishwasher and the reason why I want to give it as a gift is the [steam function]. Sentence (English): I like our new Bosch dishwasher but the loading patterns are completely different from anything we've had before.
Comments (English): [ Still learning to load it ] || ---------------- || I like our new Bosch dishwasher but the loading patterns are completely different from anything we've had before. While there are loading guides, what we actually use doesn't lend itself to those tidy pictures.We use lots of reusable plastic containers, so those tend to take up the entire second shelf. I lift the stemware holders and rest them on the top of small cups to stop them from turning over. Those not held down do turn over more frequently than I'd like.I love the top shelf flatware holder. I haven't had occasion to push its capacity but chessy forks come out perfectly clean.The bottom rack properly holds bowls that were a problem with previous dishwashers. With two directions to work from, I'm still playing around with exactly what goes where and when but we're getting there. Being able to adjust the spaces between the tines is a big plus.Our only caution about this machine is to carefully measure counter depth before purchasing. Our house is 18 years old and the counters are not quite deep enough to cover the top controls fully. We've having to be extra careful not to get water on the controls.

Sentence (English): So far, dishwasher works well: washes, dries (reasonably) and is very quiet; the rack organization is reasonable.
Comments (English): So far, dishwasher works well: washes, dries (reasonably) and is very quiet; the rack organization is reasonable. However, there are a few significant problematic points: First, setting up Home Connect was quite painful – the process of using Bluetooth to connect the device, wifi and my phone was excruciating. The basic instructions are extremely primitive. Only after endless hours of troubleshooting and research, I discovered that a. my phone needed to be on wifi only – i.e., the wireless phone carrier signal needed to be turned off, and b. my extender needed to be turned off (or renamed). Who naturally has their phone on wifi only? And many people use extenders that don't have a separate name from their router. And while this was not my issue, the DW will only work on 2.4GHz, not 5 GHz. And when you finally can detect the router, the setup shows only the router with the best connection (if you live in an apartment building, there can be a dozen other routers with stronger signals than yours) – to see the other ones, you have to click on that router; this also is not obvious at all. These are such common traps that they should be presented upfront and obviously, and should not simply buried in FAQ. Better yet fix the set-up so that these aren't issues. Many might be just as happy to not use Home Connect, but the extra featured cycles (that you pay for if you have a 300, 500, 800+) are available only thru the app – extremely annoying. Next, and probably the bigger issue, since the former was solvable, when the dishwasher runs it emits a harsh chemical odor, which after some online research, is best identified as a tar smell. At first I thought burning rubber, and got very concerned, but there was no smoking or visible haze. It seems numerous users have encountered a similar smell over the years and they identify it as the result of bitumen (an asphalt related substance) in the insulation heating up during use. (Sadly, I hope this is the issue and not something even worse. It definitely is not because of food build-up or such – the smell was noticed around the third use and no food scraps go into the DW.) I hadn't noticed this the first few washes, because I set the DW and then left the kitchen. In my case, the smell dissipates relatively quickly, but it is clearly noticeable within a 3-5 feet radius – the smell comes from between the door / control panel top edge and the countertop. It seems for other users the smell can be overpowering. To try to minimize this, we typically run the DW at delicate (lower temps), eco and half-load, to reduce heat and running time. This is not a trivial issue, and seems very common. We don't need toxic chemicals in the house. It's been over 2 months, and the smell hasn't disappeared as a “new appliance” smell. I don't understand why Bosch won't correct it. Also, installation-wise there's got to be a better mounting system. The pieces included don't work for top mounting with stone / marble counters, unless you want to drill in (bad idea). The side mount doesn't work well and is very fiddly. And based on the weight distribution and the requirement of gap space, unless the DW is secured firmly, the whole appliance will tilt if you try to open the door. This is another design flaw that should be fixed. Other issues: The bottom surface of the tub has a few areas that are depressed and will collect water that sits even when the cycle is over. Given the importance of keeping the interior of tub as dry as possible to prevent mold etc., it's not clear why these areas are necessary and the design can't be adjusted. The user manual tells you that the drain hose must at some point be at least 33 inches high. But that's the dishwasher height. Most countertops will be at 34 inches. Who has the adjacent space higher than that? And most people will have the drain hose reside under the sink, where there is a sink basin. We manage to have it at about 32, but that was hard to accomplish. Bosch (or the Home Depot) should also make very clear in product presentation materials that the three prong connector is included but a separate connector must be purchased for hardwiring – it takes too much research to find this out before purchase (and it's clear others have missed it until the installers arrive). While in some respects the DW seems very good, these other issues are substantial and known (or knowable) and seem eminently correctable.

Who naturally has their phone on wifi only? And many people use extenders that don't have a separate name from their router. And while this was not my issue, the DW will only work on 2.4GHz, not 5 GHz. And when you finally can detect the router, the setup shows only the router with the best connection (if you live in an apartment building, there can be a dozen other routers with stronger signals than yours) – to see the other ones, you have to click on that router; this also is not obvious at all. These are such common traps that they should be presented upfront and obviously, and should not simply buried in FAQ. Better yet fix the set-up so that these aren't issues. The pieces included don't work for top mounting with stone / marble counters, unless you want to drill in (bad idea). The side mount doesn't work well and is very fiddly. And based on the weight distribution and the requirement of gap space, unless the DW is secured firmly, the whole appliance will tilt if you try to open the door. Who has the adjacent space higher than that? And most people will have the drain hose reside under the sink, where there is a sink basin. We manage to have it at about 32, but that was hard to accomplish. Sentence (English): I bought this to replace my previous KitchenAid dishwasher of the same trim level.
Comments (English): [ 4.5 out of 5 Old Model vs. New ] || ---------------- || I bought this to replace my previous KitchenAid dishwasher of the same trim level. The previous one worked well over 8 years of heavy use and I still was able to sell that one for $100 to partially pay for this one. The new one looks almost identical on the outside except the vent is now moved to the front in the form of a small slit. This is likely an improvement as I was worried the side vent on the old one which looked cool sort of like shark gills, would eventually damage the cabinet from humidity. The old one also had a tendency to intake small tomato seeds that would go through the system and lodge in the spray bar, this one does not and cleans very well so far. The new one is not quite as sturdily built as the old one the frame seems lighter and the motor smaller but once installed correctly it all works. The old one had a made in the USA sticker at the kick guard the new one does not so I hope the new one was mostly USA built thats part of why I went with the brand. Overall it looks great and cleans great, better than the old model. Control touch buttons are improved. I would give it 4.5 out of 5 my main complaint is that during install the direction diagrams could be improved and my main issue was there were supposed to be side mount screws provided with it, but the holes for the side mount are not countersunk and the tolerance of the door is so tight that I can't see how you could mount via side screws without some special screw that was not provided. That drove me crazy as it was very difficult to get square in the cabinet. The old one just had two screw holes in the side very easy I don't understand the change so if you have to mount from the side (if you have stone countertop) call tech support or good luck.

The new one looks almost identical on the outside except the vent is now moved to the front in the form of a small slit. This is likely an improvement as I was worried the side vent on the old one which looked cool sort of like shark gills, would eventually damage the cabinet from humidity. The old one also had a tendency to intake small tomato seeds that would go through the system and lodge in the spray bar, this one does not and cleans very well so far. The new one is not quite as sturdily built as the old one the frame seems lighter and the motor smaller but once installed correctly it all works. The old one had a made in the USA sticker at the kick guard the new one does not so I hope the new one was mostly USA built thats part of why I went with the brand. Overall it looks great and cleans great, better than the old model. Control touch buttons are improved. I would give it 4.5 out of 5 my main complaint is that during install the direction diagrams could be improved and my main issue was there were supposed to be side mount screws provided with it, but the holes for the side mount are not countersunk and the tolerance of the door is so tight that I can’t see how you could mount via side screws without some special screw that was not provided. That drove me crazy as it was very difficult to get square in the cabinet. The old one just had two screw holes in the side very easy I don’t understand the change so if you have to mount from the side (if you have stone countertop) call tech support or good luck.

Sentence (English): I like our new Bosch dishwasher but the loading patterns are completely different from anything we've had before.
Comments (English): [ Still learning to load it ] || ---------------- || I like our new Bosch dishwasher but the loading patterns are completely different from anything we've had before. While there are loading guides, what we actually use doesn't lend itself to those tidy pictures. We use lots of reusable plastic containers, so those tend to take up the entire second shelf. I lift the stemware holders and rest them on the top of small cups to stop them from turning over. Those not held down do turn over more frequently than I'd like. I love the top shelf flatware holder. I haven't had occasion to push its capacity but chessy forks come out perfectly clean. The bottom rack properly holds bowls that were a problem with previous dishwashers. With two directions to work from, I'm still playing around with exactly what goes where and when but we're getting there. Being able to adjust the spaces between the tines is a big plus. Our only caution about this machine is to carefully measure counter depth before purchasing. Our house is 18 years old and the counters are not quite deep enough to cover the top controls fully. We've having to be extra careful not to get water on the controls.

Comments (English): [ Okay, but not as expected ] || ---------------- || Based on the test results from Stiftung Warentest, I would have expected a significantly better product. The first thing you have to deal with is the assembly instructions. The QR code with the help videos are well done, but the rest of the assembly instructions could be improved - everything is far too small and confusing. The machine itself is okay, but the capacity is even worse than our 18 year old Neff machine. With a cutlery tray at the top and large plates at the bottom (i.e. the norm), you cannot adjust the middle basket down so far that capacity can be used for large glasses or the double tier for small cups. This is just bad! The cutlery on the top shelf is usually not completely clean, even though we only use every third grid. Well, the dishes and/or the plastic aren't super dry either. I think the Home Connect version is good, but that's not why we bought it :-/

Die Maschine selbst ist okay, aber die Kapazität ist selbst schlecht als unsere 18 Jahre alte Neff Maschine. Mit Besteckkasten oben und großen Tellern unten drin (also der Regelfall) kann man den mittleren Korb nicht so weit nach unten justieren, dass Kapazität für große Gläser oder der Doppelstock für kleine Tassen nutzbar ist. Das ist einfach schlecht! Auch ist das Besteck in der oberen Ablage meist nicht komplett sauber, wenngleich wir nur jedes dritte Raster nutzen. Naja, und super trocken ist das Geschirr und/oder das Plastik auch nicht. Gut finde ich die Home Connect Variante, aber deswegen hatten wir ihn ja nicht gekauft :-/

Sentence (English): I was blown away when I realized my brand new LG dishwasher DID NOT DRY THE DISHES !
Comments (English): [ AVOID THIS MACHINE AT ALL COSTS . BELIEVE ME. ] || ---------------- || I was blown away when I realized my brand new LG dishwasher DID NOT DRY THE DISHES ! It does indeed wash the dishes but does not DRY the dishes . you need to do that yourself. Kind of like living with a roommate. In this day and age I never thought this was a possibility. The LG technician informed me that the unit has a very small heater and that I NEEDED TO RUN MY TAP WATER TO GET THE WATER UP TO TEMPERATURE BEFORE USING THE MACHINE. To my mind, this counteracts ANY water savings this new unit might offer. It appears that the unit relies on customer added additional chemicals to "drip dry" the dishes. This not only adds to the cost of use and requires over night wash times, but puts additional chemicals out into the environment. This is just crazy. I spent close to $800 and I now have a brand new machine that does not perform as well as the ten year old unit it replaces. There is NO WAY I could ever tell a friend in good faith to buy this machine . unless they really liked standing in the kitchen and towel drying their dishes. I'm not trying to be a jerk about this but $800 is a lot of money these days, not to mention the hassle of installation . My new car parks itself so it NEVER crossed my mind that in 2023 a new dishwasher would not dry the dishes.

Sentence (English): Dishwashing supplies: dishwashing salt (for soft water), rinse agent (quick drying after adding), dishwashing powder (cleaning effect).
Comments (English): Dishwashing supplies: dishwashing salt (for soft water), rinse agent (quick drying after adding), dishwashing powder (cleaning effect). The first two are added once and last for a long time. The dishwashing powder needs to be added every time. I didn't add the first two in the first wash, and only used 3-in-1. It was a little wet after washing. Later, I added the first two and used the intensive mode, and it was indeed very dry. I feel that the three-in-one is an enhanced version of dishwashing powder, but it cannot replace salt and rinsing agent. Note that the instructions say to add 500ml of water for the first time and then pour 500g of salt, but the salt is full. So it is recommended to put less water first~ My model can be connected to the app and you can see the temperature of each mode. The commonly used intensified 65-degree temperature can wash plastic products, which is very clean. I washed all the crisper lids and glasses at home. It enhances happiness so much that I regret buying it too late!
Comments (Original): 洗碗耗材:洗碗盐(软水用的)漂洗剂(加了很快烘干)洗碗粉(清洁功效)其中前两个加一次用好久，洗碗粉每次都要加。我第一次洗没加前两个，只用了三合一，洗完有点挂水，后来加了前两个之后用了强化模式，果然特别干。我感觉三合一是强化版的洗碗粉，但是也代替不了盐和漂洗剂还有注意说明书里说的是第一次加盐先加500ml水再倒500g盐，结果盐满出来了。所以建议先少放点水~我这个型号可以连接app，可以看到每个模式的温度。常用的加强65度可以洗塑料制品，特别干净，把家里的保鲜盒盖子和玻璃杯全洗了一遍。太提升幸福感了，后悔买晚了!

Still, saved $300. Tray rollers are cheaper plastic but guess they won't rust. Inner door surface seems to remain moist even after a couple days last use, which seemed odd, but no ill side effects so far with that.

Comments (English): [ So Far So Good ] || ---------------- || We bought a Bosch dishwasher based upon a relative's positive experience. So far so good after a month's use. The controls on the front are easy to see (although it would be nice if the far left on/off button and the far right start buttons were lit also) and it feels solid. Washes so far have been good and dishes and utensil feel very clean even on the normal/most energy efficient cycle. It has a built-in water softener; I have this turned off as our city water is very soft, but you will need to buy special Finish dishwasher salt if you have harder water. Best of all, it is very quiet (except when water drains into our sink plumbing drain, which is typical of about any dishwasher). Only minor complaint so far is that the third/top rack is not very deep, so can't put anything in it other than silverware, a few plastic lids and very thin kitchen utensils (our relative's Bosch has a much deeper third rack). The second rack is adjustable height however, which is handy.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher is very quiet and cleans most moderate level burnt on stains on utensils.
Comments (English): [ Practical features but has installation nuances ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher is very quiet and cleans most moderate level burnt on stains on utensils. The rack tines have enough customisation and flexibility to fit larger items. The drying and cleaning ability is ver good for both plastic, metallic and glass items. The ability to customise 4 zones on the bottom rack from the app is pretty nice. It helps focus cleaning for the extra dirty utensils irrespective of its placements. The control panel responsiveness would be better. The outer insulation is not fitted too well (does not impact sound and but just expected a more clean cut and better fit from factory at this price point. The drain outlet, water inlet and power connections are all at the back. Make sure to have the power outlet plug point very close to the dishwasher (preferably on right) otherwise wiring length is pretty limited. A sense of a plug point would require the junction box sold by Bosch as this dishwasher uses custom connectors at its backside vs plain wires. Adjusting the height of the dishwasher legs is quite finicky post installation ( make sure you adjust the feet prior). Overall a good purchase for a solid built product.

Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher. very quiet! ] || ---------------- || Bought this to replace our 15 year old Whirlpool dishwasher that died but worked well its entire life. This new model is so quiet and has a third drawer/shelf for large utensils, lids etc and the second (middle) shelf is height adjustable, which is handy for our long stemmed wine glasses. The utensil basket on the bottom drawer is removable which is a great feature. Dishes come out clean as long as you load dishwasher according to Whirlpool's guidelines. Have had it 6 months now and no issues whatsoever. Oh almost forget to mention, how much I love how the new stainless steel finish doesn't show fingerprints! The only minor negatives with this machine are 1. It goes through about 20% more rinse-aid fluid, although our dishes and glassware come out more sparkly clean than before, and 2. as others have mentioned it takes longer to go through an entire wash cycle but we always put our washer on just before going to bed each night so for us, so not an issue for our family. The quick cycle option is there if you need it and we have tried it and it works fine for a standard load of dirty dishes but not if you have really dirty, with cooked on debris, soiled pots, then this cycle won't cut it.
